scenario.title: Equipment-Specific Measurement Workflow
scenario.initial_description: A wafer is measured using one of several tools. The exact preparation and measurement steps differ by tool, and the engineer records the result after measurement.

reference_workflow.goal: Measure a wafer using the appropriate equipment-specific procedure and record the result.

activities.name: Confirm measurement request and wafer identifier
Check equipment availability and reserve slot
Prepare wafer according to equipment procedure

decisions.condition: Which equipment is required for the requested measurement?
Is the equipment available and qualified?

automation_opportunities.rationale: Equipment selection can be recommended from measurement type and wafer condition.
Reservation checks can be automated through system integration.
Output validity can be partially checked using rule-based thresholds or historical patterns.

decisions.condition: Which measurement tool is selected for this wafer?
Is the measurement result valid and within expected range?
Can the exception be resolved by re-measurement?

exceptions: Tool unavailable or under maintenance at time of measurement request
Measurement data out of expected range requiring re-measurement
Engineer unavailable to validate results in required timeframe
Incomplete or missing work order information at intake

automation_opportunities.rationale: Tool selection can be automated by querying real-time tool availability and matching measurement type requirements to tool capabilities, reducing manual decision-making and wait time.
constraints: Requires live integration with tool scheduling or equipment management system
Must handle edge cases where no suitable tool is available

automation_opportunities.rationale: Once tool selection logic is automated, the routing decision can be handled programmatically based on the selected tool ID, eliminating manual branching.
constraints: Routing rules must be explicitly encoded and maintained

automation_opportunities.rationale: Many precision measurement tools support programmatic recipe execution and automated data capture via APIs or standard protocols, removing the need for manual operation.
required_data: Measurement recipe or parameters per tool
Tool API or control interface specification
constraints: Tool integration capability varies by tool model and age
Requires validated and version-controlled measurement recipes
May require regulatory or quality approval for automated operation

automation_opportunities.target: A5 - Review and Validate Measurement Output
automation_opportunities.rationale: Automated range checking and statistical validation against predefined thresholds can flag out-of-range results without manual review, accelerating throughput.
required_data: Expected value ranges per measurement type
constraints: Edge cases requiring engineering judgment may still need human review
Threshold definitions must be maintained and version-controlled
False-positive rate must be acceptable to operations team

automation_opportunities.rationale: Validated results can be automatically written to the lab information management system upon passing validation, eliminating manual data entry and reducing transcription errors.
required_data: LIMS write API or integration endpoint
constraints: Requires reliable integration between validation layer and LIMS
Data format standardization across tools required
Audit trail and traceability requirements must be preserved

automation_opportunities.rationale: Automated exception triage can categorize failure types, log exceptions, and trigger re-measurement requests or escalation notifications without waiting for engineer intervention.
constraints: Complex or novel exceptions may still require human judgment
Escalation workflows must be defined and agreed upon in advance

automation_opportunities.rationale: Wafer intake and work order validation can be partially automated through barcode or RFID scanning combined with automated work order lookup, reducing manual logging.
constraints: Requires physical scanning infrastructure at intake station
Work order system must be accessible in real time

assumptions: Three representative tools (Tool A, Tool B, Tool C) are used as placeholders; the actual number and types of tools may vary.
Each tool has a distinct preparation protocol and measurement procedure that differs meaningfully from the others.
A lab information management system or equivalent data repository exists for storing measurement results.
Tool availability and scheduling information is tracked in some form of lab tracking or equipment management system.
Engineers are responsible for both preparation and measurement steps, with no separate technician role assumed unless specified.
Measurement result validation involves comparison against predefined expected ranges or specifications.
Re-measurement is a permitted resolution path for failed or out-of-range results, subject to limits.
The workflow is repeated per wafer; batch processing is not assumed unless specified.
Frequency of measurements is not specified and is assumed to be regular but variable based on production demand.
Tools may support some degree of digital interface or data export, enabling at least partial automation of measurement execution and data capture.

missing_information.gap: No criteria defined for how a specific tool is selected for a given wafer measurement
missing_information.why_it_matters: Without knowing the tool selection logic (e.g., based on wafer type, lot priority, tool availability, measurement type), it is impossible to model the branching logic or assess whether tool assignment can be automated

missing_information.gap: It is unclear who initiates the measurement request and whether multiple roles are involved across tool preparation and result recording
missing_information.why_it_matters: Automation scope depends on knowing which actors perform which steps; if preparation and recording are done by different roles, handoff points and potential bottlenecks must be identified

missing_information.gap: No information provided about the systems or interfaces used by the tools or for recording results
missing_information.why_it_matters: Automation feasibility depends on whether tools expose APIs, generate structured output files, or require manual data entry; without this, integration constraints cannot be assessed

missing_information.gap: The specific preparation steps per tool are not described, nor are the inputs required for each (e.g., recipes, calibration parameters, wafer identifiers)
missing_information.why_it_matters: Each tool variant may require different inputs, and undocumented preparation steps represent hidden manual effort and potential failure points that must be captured for accurate process modeling

missing_information.gap: The format, structure, and destination of the recorded measurement result are not specified
missing_information.why_it_matters: If results are recorded in free text, a spreadsheet, or a proprietary format, data extraction and downstream automation will require different approaches; structured vs. unstructured output significantly changes automation complexity

missing_information.gap: No exception handling is described for scenarios such as tool unavailability, measurement failure, out-of-specification results, or calibration errors
missing_information.why_it_matters: Exception paths are critical for robust automation; unhandled exceptions will cause process failures or require unplanned manual intervention, undermining automation reliability

missing_information.gap: The volume and frequency of measurements (per shift, per day, per lot) and the distribution across tools are unknown
missing_information.why_it_matters: Frequency and load distribution determine the ROI justification for automation and inform decisions about parallelism, scheduling, and resource allocation

missing_information.gap: The time spent on preparation versus measurement versus result recording per tool is not quantified
missing_information.why_it_matters: Without effort estimates per step and per tool, it is not possible to prioritize which subprocess to automate first or to calculate expected time savings

missing_information.gap: It is unclear whether measurement must follow a specific upstream process step or whether there are sequencing constraints between tools
missing_information.why_it_matters: Upstream dependencies affect when the workflow can be triggered and whether automation can proceed autonomously or must wait for external conditions to be met

missing_information.gap: It is not known whether historical measurement logs or tool usage records exist in a structured, queryable form
missing_information.why_it_matters: Process mining and automation assessment rely on historical event data; if logs are incomplete or unstructured, conformance checking and variant analysis will be severely limited

missing_information.gap: No approval or quality review step is mentioned after result recording, nor is it clear whether out-of-spec results trigger an escalation workflow
missing_information.why_it_matters: If results require engineer sign-off or trigger corrective actions, these steps must be included in the process model; omitting them would produce an incomplete and potentially non-compliant automation design

clarification_questions.question: What criteria determine which tool is selected for a given wafer measurement — for example, is the decision based on wafer type, measurement specification, tool availability, or engineer preference, and is this decision documented anywhere?
Can you walk through the specific preparation and measurement steps for each tool variant, and identify which of those steps require manual physical interaction versus software or parameter entry?
Where and in what format does the engineer record the measurement result — for example, a paper log, spreadsheet, MES system, or tool-generated report — and is that data accessible programmatically?
What happens when a measurement result is out of specification or when a tool fails mid-measurement — is there a defined escalation or rework path, and who is responsible for that decision?
Approximately how many measurements are performed per shift or per day across all tools, and how evenly is the workload distributed between them?
Are there existing digital logs or event records from the measurement tools or surrounding systems that capture timestamps, tool IDs, wafer IDs, and outcomes in a structured format?
